summary: A 398-unit, two-phase affordable housing development at 1290 3rd St on Mission Bay South Block 4-East, bounded by Mission Rock, Third and China Basin Streets, being developed by Curtis Development and Bayview Senior Services (Phase I through Mission Bay 4 East Associates, L.P.; Phase II through Mission Bay 4 East Associates 2, L.P.). OCII authorized an Exclusive Negotiations Agreement with them on September 3, 2024, with a term through September 3, 2027; as of OCII's February 3, 2026 resolutions, the Phase I ground lease and permanent loan agreement were still to be approved. Phase I (165 units, ~160 ft) is on the southern half of the block, facing China Basin St; Phase II (233 units, ~225 ft) is on the northern half, facing Mission Rock St.

milestones.text: OCII issues a Request for Qualifications for a developer team for Block 4-East.
Four development teams respond to OCII's RFQ (event: the responses; OCII's May 21, 2024 memo says "four responses in January 2024").

OCII's evaluation panel interviews all four RFQ teams ("All four (4) teams were interviewed by the evaluation panel on February 21, 2024"). The panel's selection of the Curtis Development / Bayview Senior Services team came after these interviews; the memo gives no date for the pick itself.

OCII's Executive Director sends the Commission an informational memorandum recommending the team led by Curtis Development and Bayview Senior Services, with Y.A. studio as lead architect and The John Stewart Company as property manager (the team also presented to the Mission Bay Citizens Advisory Committee on May 9, 2024).

OCII Commission Resolution No. 30-2024 authorizes the Executive Director to enter into an Exclusive Negotiations Agreement and a Loan Agreement with an affiliate of Curtis Development and Bayview Senior Services, "provid[ing] funding of up to $5,111,731" for predevelopment (as recited in Resolution No. 02-2026; the staff memo recommending it names Mission Bay 4 East Associates, L.P. as the borrower and gives the ENA term as through September 3, 2027). The $5,111,731 is a ceiling, not money spent.

OCII Commission Resolution No. 02-2026 authorizes commitment of approximately $89,600,000 in permanent gap loan funds for Phase I (165 units); the concurrent Resolution No. 03-2026 authorizes a $5,000,000 Phase I predevelopment loan agreement that is "inclusive of $1,943,150.16 in funds expended as of December 16, 2025" under the 2024 predevelopment loan (Exhibit A), so it replaces rather than adds to that spending. Resolution No. 04-2026 (headed "Adopted February 3, 2026") authorizes a $5,000,000 Phase II predevelopment loan to Mission Bay 4 East Associates 2, L.P., likewise inclusive of $1,749,266 spent as of December 16, 2025.

Tentative Parcel Map No. 12743 is dated March 31, 2026 (the date on the map, per the Notice of Exemption, not a subdivision event); it proposes to subdivide Assessor Block 8711, Lot 029B into two lots for Phase I and Phase II. It is a tentative map: no final map was found, and DataSF's parcel layer still lists 8711029B as one active lot when queried on 2026-10-12.

SF Public Works issues notice, on April 2, 2026, of its approval (Public Works Order No. 212730) of Tentative Parcel Map No. 12743 for Block 4-East; the Notice of Exemption does not give the order's own date. The approval is of a tentative map, which does not itself create the lots. The appeal period ended April 12, 2026 with no appeals filed.

A CEQA Notice of Exemption is filed for the Block 4-East project (statutory exemption under AB 1449 / Public Resources Code section 21080.40, the 100%-affordable-housing exemption). The notice states that all residential units "will be dedicated to lower-income households (earning no more than 70% of Area Median Income" on a HUD and TCAC basis, excluding unrestricted manager units, and that the project "is subject to recorded TCAC Regulatory Agreements prior to the issuance of building permits" (future tense: the agreements are to be recorded). Resolution No. 02-2026 gives two manager's units in each phase.

Phase I construction start targeted for early 2027 (Q1 2027 on the schedule), conditional: the developer's own project site says "Pending financing availability, Phase I of the development—165 apartments—will begin construction in early 2027". OCII's schedule of performance (Exhibit L to Resolution No. 03-2026) lists an estimated Notice to Proceed of February 2027, with a contractual deadline of August 2027. Both are expected dates.

Phase II construction start targeted for 2028 (the developer's own project site: Q1 2028; OCII's schedule of performance, Exhibit L to Resolution No. 04-2026: estimated Notice to Proceed February 2028). Both are expected dates.

details.text: Developer: the April 2026 Notice of Exemption names Curtis Development and Bayview Senior Services as the Developers. The development entities are Mission Bay 4 East Associates, L.P. for Phase I (OCII staff memo, September 2024; Resolution No. 02-2026) and Mission Bay 4 East Associates 2, L.P. for Phase II (Resolution No. 04-2026).

Units by phase: Phase I has 165 units (163 affordable + 2 manager units, ~160 ft, China Basin St frontage); Phase II has 233 units (231 affordable + 2 manager units, ~225 ft, Mission Rock St frontage).

Parcel number: 8711029B (1290 3rd St) was confirmed via DataSF's Parcels - Active and Retired dataset. Tentative Parcel Map No. 12743 (dated 2026-03-31, approved by SF Public Works notice of 2026-04-02) would divide it into separate Phase I and Phase II lots; the lot is not yet subdivided in DataSF, which still lists 8711029B as one active lot.

open_questions: Whether the final parcel map has been recorded: the CEQA Notice of Exemption covers only the tentative map, and DataSF's parcels layer showed lots 8711029A and 8711029B (active) and no new lots for Block 4-East on 2026-10-12, so the Phase I and Phase II lots do not yet exist as separate Assessor parcels.

Affordability figures differ across sources and are not reconciled: the April 2026 CEQA Notice of Exemption says all residential units other than manager units "will be dedicated to lower-income households (earning no more than 70% of Area Median Income" (HUD and TCAC basis); the September 2024 ENA staff memo says 30-80% of AMI as defined by MOHCD, with a subset up to 95% MOHCD AMI; the developer's own project site (mb4e.com, undated, and mentioning a July 1, 2026 event) says 35% to approximately 95% of the area's median income. The binding restriction will be the TCAC regulatory agreements, which the Notice of Exemption says are to be recorded before building permits; no recorded agreement was found.

Construction start and completion dates are all expected dates, not events. The developer's own project site (mb4e.com, undated) gives Phase I construction start Q1 2027 and completion Q2 2029, Phase II start Q1 2028 and completion Q3 2030, pending financing. OCII's schedules of performance (Exhibit L to Resolutions 03-2026 and 04-2026) give estimated Notice to Proceed of February 2027 (Phase I) and February 2028 (Phase II) and estimated Certificate of Final Completion and Occupancy of July 2029 and October 2030.

Two of the February 2026 resolutions name the Phase I borrower "Mission Bay 4 Associates, L.P." (Resolution No. 02-2026's recital on the concurrent Phase I loan, and the resolving clause of Resolution No. 03-2026), apparently a slip; the September 2024 staff memo, the operative clause of Resolution No. 02-2026 and the loan agreement in Exhibit A to Resolution No. 03-2026 name it "Mission Bay 4 East Associates, L.P.", the name used here.

No public official's or community group's stated position on the project as a whole has been found and sourced. OCII's September 2024 staff memo records that OCII staff presented the recommended developer to the Mission Bay Citizens Advisory Committee on May 9, 2024 and "the MB CAC had no objections".

OCII's September 2024 staff memo and its attached RFQ say the site "is currently in use as a temporary parking lot without any structures" and "is currently serving as a surface parking lot", with termination of the parking operator's lease "anticipated for early 2027"; these are 2024 statements, and Pier & Point's own on-site observation of a parking lot on 2026-09-13 is not a published source. No cited document says whether the project is administratively separate from the Giants/Tishman Speyer Mission Rock masterplan; the memo mentions only modeling "bulk and tower separation restrictions similar to those applied to the Mission Rock project".

A City Spring 2026 development forecast was cited for the same schedule, but its document is no longer available at the published address and could not be read; the construction start dates rest on the developer's own site (mb4e.com: Phase I Q1 2027, Phase II Q1 2028, pending financing).
